T: A long way home. A good meal waiting.
D: A boy lost thousands of kilometres from home in India is adopted in Tasmania and searches for his family as an adult.
P: Serve dessert when Saroo sees the jalebi at the party in Melbourne.
S: lost on the streets of Kolkata
Potato and pea filling with cumin, chilli and garam masala folded into pastry cones, fried at 175C until blistered. Tamarind chutney.
growing up with his new family in Hobart
Tasmanian smoked salmon folded onto buttered rye, topped with crème fraîche whipped with lemon zest, a few capers, fresh dill and a crack of black pepper.
the train that carries him far from home

Crumbly Indian shortbread biscuits with cardamom, ghee and pistachio, baked pale and cracked on top, served with small cups of hot sweet chai. Beat 100g ghee with 100g icing sugar until fluffy. Mix in 150g plain flour, 30g fine semolina, half a teaspoon of ground cardamom and a pinch of baking powder. Roll into 16 balls, press a pistachio on each and bake at 170C for 15 minutes until pale and cracked. Simmer 500ml water with 2 tbsp loose black tea, ginger and 4 crushed cardamom pods for 3 minutes, add 500ml milk and sugar, simmer 2 minutes and strain.
M: the family he left behind in a small village
Yellow split peas simmered with turmeric until soft, tempered with ghee, cumin seeds, garlic and dried chilli, served with basmati and flatbreads.
Hobart roast lamb with honey roast veg

Tasmanian lamb leg roasted with garlic and rosemary, with honey-roasted carrots, parsnips and potatoes, peas and a rich pan gravy. Heat the oven to 220C. Stud a 2kg lamb leg with garlic and rosemary, rub with oil and salt and roast 20 minutes, then at 180C for 60 minutes. Toss 1kg potatoes, 3 carrots and 2 parsnips in oil and 1 tbsp honey and roast alongside for the last hour. Rest the lamb 20 minutes. Make gravy with the tray juices, 1 tbsp flour and 400ml stock. Cook 300g peas and carve.
W: the sweet that brings his memory back
Batter of flour, yoghurt and a pinch of saffron rested overnight, piped in spirals into 170C oil, fried crisp, soaked in warm cardamom and saffron sugar syrup.
K: Black tea simmered with milk, sugar, cardamom, ginger, cinnamon and clove for 5 minutes, strained into cups.

s.note: lost on the streets of Kolkata
s.how: Boil 600g potatoes, then crush with 150g peas, cumin, chilli and garam masala. Make a firm dough of flour, oil and water, roll into rounds, cut in half and fold into cones. Fill, seal and fry at 175C until blistered and golden. Serve with tamarind chutney.

s.note: growing up with his new family in Hobart
s.how: Butter 4 slices of rye bread and cut into small pieces. Whip 200ml creme fraiche with the zest of a lemon. Top each piece with a fold of smoked salmon, a spoon of the cream, a few capers and a sprig of dill. Finish with cracked black pepper.

m.note: the family he left behind in a small village
m.how: Simmer 300g yellow split peas with a teaspoon of turmeric in plenty of water for 45 minutes until soft. In a small pan, heat 2 tbsp ghee and fry cumin seeds, sliced garlic and a dried chilli until fragrant, then pour over the dal. Serve with basmati rice.

w.note: the sweet that brings his memory back
w.how: Mix 200g flour, 100g yoghurt, a pinch of saffron and water into a thick batter and rest overnight. Boil 300g sugar with 200ml water, cardamom and saffron for 5 minutes. Pipe spirals into 170C oil, fry until crisp and soak in the warm syrup for a minute.

d.how: Bring 500ml water to the boil with a few crushed cardamom pods, sliced ginger, a cinnamon stick and a clove. Add 4 tea bags and simmer for 2 minutes. Pour in 500ml milk and sugar to taste, simmer for 5 minutes more, then strain into small cups.
